# FAQ and event details

## FAQ

**Which models can I use?** The hosted models are free, and the starter kit shows how to call them. Or bring your own key for
any provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Fireworks, or others the
organizers add) and send its calls through the metering proxy. `GET /v1/runs/current` lists the proxy base URLs. Models must have a published
price (OpenRouter reports its own) and satisfy any organizer model allowlist. See
[the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls) for SDK setup.

**Where do I keep my model key?** As a [team secret](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#team-secrets): the team page's Secrets list
injects it into your agent's run step in test and scored runs, redacted from logs. Don't put keys in your
package; we store packages and the review agent reads them.

**Why does my model call get a 401?** "Add your OpenAI API key to the request" means no provider key arrived: set
`OPENAI_API_KEY` (in test and scored runs, as a [team secret](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#team-secrets)). A 401 from the
provider itself means the key is wrong. Check that `OPENAI_BASE_URL` points at the run's proxy
(`$LLM_PROXY_URL/openai/v1`, already set in test and scored runs); the same holds for any OpenAI-compatible provider.

**How do my teammates and I sign in from a terminal?** Each person runs `atira login` on their own computer
and approves it in the browser. Every device gets its own token; there is no shared team key to pass around.
Without a browser on the machine, `atira login --device` prints a link and a code to approve elsewhere.

**I lost a laptop, or a token leaked.** Revoke that device's token on your team page under Signed-in devices
(`atira logout` revokes the one on the computer you are at). Leaving or being removed from a team ends your
tokens' access to it at once.

**My invite link says it is for someone else.** Invites are for one GitHub account. Sign in with the account
the captain invited, or ask the captain to invite your GitHub username.

**Does it cost me anything?** We charge nothing, and the models the platform hosts are free and never charged. If
you bring your own key for another provider, that provider bills your key. The proxy measures every call and
ranks you on its cost at the published prices; hosted calls count at simulated API prices.

**How can I try my agent?** Develop locally against the public websites (`atira scout --env` exports the
scouting logins), then test in the sandbox (`atira test-run ./my-agent`). A test run runs on `public-1`, the public
RFQ scenario, and returns your score with the points for each part of the answer. With the scouting logins nothing
counts: a bid entered on the tender portal is acknowledged without counting.

**Is the public scenario's answer published?** No. The correct answer isn't published; your system has to work it
out from the websites. Score breakdowns show the points for each part of the answer, never the expected values.

**Which submission counts?** Your best submission holds your place on the leaderboard, which ranks scored runs on
the public dataset. Your latest one that passed review (not your best one) goes into the final run: when the
hackathon ends, the organizers run it once by default (or best of three if you opt in before the final run starts) on a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software, with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it.
That run weighs most when we pick the winners, ahead of your public score and the elegance of your system, so
build an agent that works the answer out from the websites, not one tuned to the public scenario. See
[Winners](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#winners).

**Why did my answer get a 400?** It does not match `answer_schema`. The response lists the issues; the run is
still open, so fix it and send it again.

**Can I run my agent outside the sandbox?** While you develop, yes, anywhere, with the scouting logins. Test runs
and scored runs always run in our sandbox.

**Why is my run still queued?** Runs share the sandboxes in a fair order: scored runs first, then teams take turns,
the team with the fewest runs in flight first. Your team runs up to 5 test runs at a time and can have up to 3
waiting; the next waits while other teams' runs start. The run page says how many runs are ahead of yours, and
`atira test-run --follow` prints it. See [the run queue](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md#the-run-queue).

**How do I stop a run?** `atira cancel <run>`, or Cancel run on its run page. The sandbox is removed, the run fails
with "Cancelled by @you", and you can start the next test run at once. A cancelled scored run ends its
submission: the leaderboard ignores it, and you can submit again.

**Why do my requests get a 403 "Error 1010"?** The edge in front of our hosts refuses some default HTTP
clients, such as Python's `urllib`. Send your own `User-Agent` header (the starter kit does).

**Python says `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED` on my Mac.** Python from python.org ships without CA certificates.
Run `Install Certificates.command` from its folder in Applications, or set `SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/cert.pem`.

**What can my agent reach during a scored run?** Our API (including the model proxy) and the challenge's
websites, nothing else. The `HTTP(S)_PROXY` variables in the run's environment route there; Python's
`urllib`, `requests`, `httpx`, the Anthropic SDK and Node's `fetch` pick them up automatically. Chromium is
already configured. Setup (`uv sync`, `npm ci`, …) has network, but nothing it starts survives into the
run.

## Event details

- The event is on 10 October 2026.
- A team has up to five people.
- A scored run has 20 minutes on the clock; a test run has up to 2 hours.
- Ask the organizers about the submission deadline and prizes.

## Final private evaluation: one attempt or best of three

The final runs your latest passed submission once, or up to three times if you opt in to **Best of 3** on your team
page before the final starts (`atira final --best-of 3`). Your best attempt counts. Details:
[Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#final-private-evaluation-one-attempt-or-best-of-three).
# Demo day

> In this document, `$API` is https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai (the CLI and API guide call it `$ATIRA_API`).

The best teams run their agent live on stage against the public scenario while the room watches the live run
view.

- **The live run view** at `$API/runs/<run id>` shows the team, a running timer, LLM calls and tokens per model,
  the cost so far, and the score once the answer is in. Its timer ticks every second and the rest refreshes every
  two seconds; it is what the projector shows.
- **Your agent's screen:** run it on your laptop with a visible browser, or in our sandbox, whose desktop we can
  show.
- **Prepare:** a one-line command that starts your agent, such as `atira test-run ./my-agent` (it opens the run
  page), a reliable network, and a fallback recording.

1	# The CLI
2	
3	A command line for taking part: one JavaScript file for Node 24 that uses only Node's built-ins. It is made for
4	people and coding agents alike: every command takes `--json`, and exit codes tell outcomes apart. Everything it does
5	is plain HTTP, described in the [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md); you never need the CLI.
6	
7	## Install
8	
9	macOS and Linux:
10	
11	```sh
12	export ATIRA_API=https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai
13	curl -fsSL "$ATIRA_API/install.sh" | sh
14	```
15	
16	Windows, in PowerShell (5.1 or 7):
17	
18	```powershell
19	$env:ATIRA_API = "https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai"
20	irm "$env:ATIRA_API/install.ps1" | iex
21	```
22	
23	The script checks for Node 24 or newer. Where it is missing, it asks whether to install a private copy for atira
24	alone, the latest Node 24 from nodejs.org, checked against the release's `SHASUMS256.txt`. It needs no admin rights
25	and never changes the `node` on your `PATH`. Without a terminal to ask in, `ATIRA_INSTALL_NODE=1` says yes (`0`, no).
26	Then it downloads `/cli.mjs`, checks it against `/cli.mjs.sha256` and installs it for you alone, without sudo:
27	
28	- macOS and Linux: the file in `~/.local/share/atira/atira.mjs`, Node (if needed) in `~/.local/share/atira/node`,
29	  and an `atira` command in `~/.local/bin`. It tells you when `~/.local/bin` is not on your `PATH`.
30	- Windows: the same under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\atira`, with `atira.cmd` in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\atira\bin`, which it adds to
31	  your user `PATH`. Open a new terminal afterwards.
32	
33	The `atira` command runs your own Node when it is 24 or newer, else the private copy. Running the installer again
34	updates the CLI; it downloads Node again only when the private copy is older than 24. Read the script first, if you
35	like:
36	
37	```sh
38	curl -fsSL "$ATIRA_API/install.sh" | less
39	```
40	
41	To uninstall: `rm -rf ~/.local/share/atira ~/.local/bin/atira`, or on Windows
42	`Remove-Item -Recurse -Force "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\atira"`. Your sign-in stays in the config file (see below) until you
43	delete it.
44	
45	Without installing anything, download the file and run it with Node; `node atira.mjs` works wherever this guide
46	says `atira`:
47	
48	```sh
49	curl -fsSL "$ATIRA_API/cli.mjs" -o atira.mjs && node atira.mjs --help
50	```
51	
52	The CLI talks to the server it was downloaded from. Set `ATIRA_API` to use another one. `atira upgrade` downloads the
53	server's current version, checks its SHA-256 and replaces the file; a download that does not match leaves the file
54	as it was.
55	
56	## Sign in
57	
58	```sh
59	atira login
60	```
61	
62	The browser opens a page that asks you to sign in with GitHub, then whether to sign in the CLI on this computer.
63	Approve, and the browser returns to the CLI, which stores a personal token for you. The token acts as you, on the
64	team you are in at the time of each request: leave the team, or be removed, and it no longer reaches the team. It
65	lasts 90 days. Your team page lists your signed-in devices; revoke any of them there.
66	
67	Where no browser can open (an SSH session, a container, a coding agent), sign in with a code instead:
68	
69	```sh
70	atira login --device
71	```
72	
73	It prints a link with the code filled in. Open it on any device, check that the code matches and approve; the CLI
74	waits and then stores the token. `atira login` switches to the code by itself when the browser cannot be opened, or
75	offers it when the browser has not answered after two minutes.
76	
77	```sh
78	atira whoami                                  # who you are, your team, and when the token expires
79	atira token                                   # the token, for curl and scripts
80	curl -H "x-api-key: $(atira token)" "$ATIRA_API/v1/teams/me"

82	```
83	
84	The token is kept per server in `~/.config/atira/config.json` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/atira/config.json`; on Windows
85	`%USERPROFILE%\.config\atira\config.json`), readable only by you (mode 0600). `ATIRA_TOKEN` overrides it, which suits
86	CI and agents: `export ATIRA_TOKEN=$(atira token)`.
87	
88	## Commands
89	
90	| Command | What it does |
91	| --- | --- |
92	| `login [--device] [--key <key>]` | Sign in through the browser, or with a code (`--device`), and store a personal token; `--key` stores a team key where there is no GitHub sign-in |
93	| `logout` | Revoke the stored token on the server and forget it |
94	| `whoami` | Who you are signed in as, your team, and when the token expires |
95	| `token` | Print the token in use, for `curl -H "x-api-key: $(atira token)"` |
96	| `upgrade` | Download the server's current CLI, check its SHA-256 and replace this file |
97	| `challenges` | The challenges, with their Markdown pages |
98	| `challenge <id>` | A challenge as Markdown: task, websites, rules, run contract, submitting, answer schema |
99	| `scout [--challenge <id>] [--env [--port <port>]]` | The published scouting logins for the public websites; `--env` prints them as shell exports for running your agent locally, with any hosted model's variables pointed at `atira models proxy`; use the same `--port` when the proxy runs on another port |
100	| `models proxy [--port <port>]` | Where the organizers host models: a local proxy to them on 127.0.0.1 (port 8765) that prints each model's base URL and key variables |
101	| `test-run <dir> [--challenge <id>] [--dry-run] [--follow] [--no-open]` | Pack a folder, run it once in the sandbox on the public dataset and open its run page; `--follow` prints its place in the queue, then streams its logs here |
102	| `submit <dir> [--challenge <id>] [--dry-run] [--follow] [--no-open]` | Pack a folder and submit it: review, then one scored run on the public dataset; opens your team page; `--follow` prints the review, each run's place in the queue and its end here |
103	| `cancel <run>` | Cancel a test or scored run that has not finished: its sandbox is removed and the run fails |
104	| `final [--best-of <1\|3>] [--challenge <id>]` | Read or change the final attempt choice before the final run starts |
105	| `status [<id>] [--challenge <id>]` | Your latest submissions and test runs, or one submission (`sub_...`), test run (`reh_...`) or run (`run_...`) |
106	| `logs <run> [--follow]` | A test or scored run's logs; `--follow` keeps polling until the run has ended |
107	| `package <id> [--out <dir>]` | The package a test run (`reh_...` or `run_...`), scored run or submission (`sub_...`) of your team used, as uploaded: agent.json and each file's size; `--out` saves the `.tar.gz` in a folder, checked against its SHA-256 |
108	| `leaderboard [--challenge <id>]` | The leaderboard |
109	| `mcp` | Serve MCP on stdio for your coding agent: list and debug runs (why one failed, logs by time, model calls, where the time went, a browser's screen at a time, recorded inputs, two runs compared), start and wait for test runs, and cancel a run or submit when you confirm ([MCP guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md)) |
110	
111	Every command accepts `--json` (machine-readable output on stdout, errors included) and `--help`.
112	`--challenge` defaults to `ATIRA_CHALLENGE`, else the platform's first challenge. While `login` waits, it writes its
113	instructions to stderr, so `--json` output on stdout stays one JSON document.
114	
115	### Develop locally, then test in the sandbox
116	
117	Develop against the public websites on your own machine, then test the package in the sandbox:
118	
119	```sh
120	atira scout                    # the scouting logins: each website, its URL, username and password
121	eval "$(atira scout --env)"    # the same as shell exports
122	uv run python agent.py         # your agent, on your machine, against the public websites (the starter kit's way)
123	atira test-run ./my-agent      # then one run in the sandbox, opened live in the browser
124	```
125	
126	On Windows, `--env` and `models proxy` print PowerShell's `$env:NAME = '...'` instead; load them with
127	`atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression`.
128	
129	### Hosted models from your machine
130	
131	Where the organizers host models, a run gets each one's base URL and key variables set for it, and the
132	Getting started page names them. On your machine, run the proxy in its own terminal: it prints the same variables,
133	pointed at itself, with `local` as the key (any non-empty value works through it).
134	
135	```sh
136	atira login                    # once per computer
137	atira models proxy             # keep it running; it prints the exports
138	```
139	
140	`eval "$(atira scout --env)"` sets the same variables with the scouting logins; it never exports your sign-in. The proxy
141	listens on 127.0.0.1 only. It holds a 30-minute inference token, good for model calls only and bound to an Ed25519 key
142	that never leaves the process, signs every call with that key and rotates the token before it expires. A copied token
143	works in no other client. Calls from your machine are free, recorded and never ranked. If port 8765 is in use, pick
144	the same port for the proxy and the scouting exports:
145	
146	```sh
147	atira models proxy --port 8777                   # in a second terminal
148	eval "$(atira scout --env --port 8777)"
149	```
150	
151	In PowerShell, the second line is `atira scout --env --port 8777 | Out-String | Invoke-Expression`. The proxy also
152	prints the command with its actual port, including when `--port 0` lets the operating system choose one.
153	
154	`scout` needs no sign-in for the logins. It prints the logins the organizers published, how long they are valid,
155	and what happens to an answer: these are demo logins, so an answer entered on the website that takes it is
156	acknowledged without counting. For RFQ, a bid entered on the tender portal is acknowledged without counting. `--json` prints what
157	`GET /v1/challenges/<id>/scouting` returns: the logins as `access`, plus `submission`, `brief` and `answer_schema`,
158	shaped like a run's `/v1/runs/current`. `--env` prints:
159	
160	| Variable | Value |
161	| --- | --- |
162	| `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING` | what `GET /v1/challenges/<id>/scouting` returned, as JSON: the brief, logins and answer format |
163	| `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING_URL` | `$ATIRA_API/v1/challenges/<id>/scouting`, the same without a token once the organizers publish the logins |
164	| `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` | the websites with the scouting logins, the JSON a run gets: `[{"siteId", "url", "credentials": {"username", "password"}}]` |
165	| `CHALLENGE_SITE_<ID>_URL` | each website's URL, its id upper-cased with `_` for other characters, e.g. `CHALLENGE_SITE_TENDER_PORTAL_URL` |
166	| `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`, `<MODEL>_API_KEY` | only when the platform hosts models: each one through `atira models proxy` on this computer, with `local` as the key. Keep the proxy running in another terminal, signed in with `atira login`. `atira scout --help` names them |
167	
168	With `--env --json`, the same variables come as one JSON object. There is no run token: your agent calls other
169	models with your own key, directly or through the model proxy with your personal token (see
170	[LLM calls](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls)). Calls through the proxy from your machine, a hosted model's included, are
171	recorded for your team and never ranked. A hosted model is free to use, never charged; each call counts toward your
172	run's cost at simulated API prices, so the cost ranking stays honest. Nothing done with these logins counts.

174	proxy: your agent starts its own browsers. When nothing is published yet, `scout` exits 4: organizers publish the scouting logins before the event.
175	
176	### Test runs and submissions
177	
178	```sh
179	atira test-run ./my-agent --dry-run   # what would be uploaded, and what is left out
180	atira test-run ./my-agent             # one run in the sandbox on the public dataset; opens its run page
181	atira test-run ./my-agent --follow    # the same, and its logs here until it ends
182	atira cancel run_...                  # stop a run that has not finished
183	atira submit ./my-agent               # review, then the scored run on the public dataset; opens your team page
184	atira status sub_...
185	```
186	
187	`test-run` uploads the package, starts the test run and, when its output goes to a terminal, opens the run page in
188	the browser: the browser, the logs, the phases and the score with its full breakdown, live. `submit` opens your team
189	page instead, which shows the submission's review and then links each scored run as it starts: the run does not

191	`ATIRA_BROWSER` picks the
192	command that opens the page (`none` only prints the link), `--no-open` skips it, and `--json` never opens anything.
193	
194	`test-run --follow` then streams the run's logs as `logs --follow` does and exits 7 if the run failed or timed out.
195	While the run waits for a sandbox, it prints its place in the [fair queue](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md#the-run-queue) on stderr whenever
196	that changes ("Queued: 3 runs ahead of yours"). With `--json --follow`, the upload's result comes as one JSON line,
197	then one `{"at", "stream", "text"}` line per chunk. `submit --follow` prints the review's outcome, then each scored
198	run's place in the queue and its end, and exits 7 unless the submission completes; with `--json`, the final
199	submission follows the upload's line.
200	
201	`cancel <run>` takes a run (`run_...`) or a test run (`reh_...`) of your team that has not finished. The run's sandbox
202	is removed and the run fails with the error "Cancelled by @you"; a queued run is cancelled before it starts. Your
203	team can start the next test run at once. A cancelled scored run leaves its submission not complete: the leaderboard
204	ignores that submission, and you can submit again. A run that
205	has already finished answers 409 (exit 6).
206	
207	`test-run` and `submit` pack the folder into a gzipped tarball the way the platform reads it:
208	
209	- `agent.json` must be at the folder's root, with `run` (and optionally `setup`) as arrays of strings.
210	- `.git`, `node_modules` and `.DS_Store` are always left out, and so is whatever `.gitignore` files exclude (in the
211	  folder and below: patterns, `*`, `?`, `**`, `[...]`, a leading `/`, a trailing `/` for folders, and `!` to
212	  include again). Symbolic links are left out too.
213	- The limits are checked before uploading: at most 2,000 files, 5 MB per file, 20 MB in total, and 20 MB
214	  compressed (or what the server announces).
215	
216	### Logs, status and the leaderboard
217	
218	`package <id>` shows exactly what a run ran: the package's SHA-256 and label, its `agent.json` and every file with
219	its size. A scored run ran its submission's package. `--out ./downloaded` also saves the `.tar.gz` there; unpack it
220	with `tar -xzf <file> -C <folder>`.
221	
222	`logs <run>` prints what the run has written so far; `--follow` polls with a growing pause (1 s, up to 10 s) and
223	exits when the run has ended. `--json` prints one `{"at", "stream", "text"}` object per line. `status` without an id
224	shows your best result, your latest submissions and your latest test runs.
225	
226	## Configuration
227	
228	| Variable | Meaning |
229	| --- | --- |
230	| `ATIRA_API` | The platform; defaults to the server the file came from |
231	| `ATIRA_TOKEN` | A token to use instead of the stored one |
232	| `ATIRA_CHALLENGE` | The default challenge |
233	| `ATIRA_POLL_MS` | The first pause of `logs --follow`, in milliseconds (default 1000) |
234	| `ATIRA_BROWSER` | The command `login`, `test-run` and `submit` open pages with, or `none` to only print the link |
235	| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | Where `atira/config.json` lives (default `~/.config`) |
236	
237	The config file holds `{"servers": {"<ATIRA_API>": {"token": "atp_...", "token_id", "expires_at", "login"}}}`.
238	
239	## Exit codes
240	
241	| Code | Meaning |
242	| --- | --- |
243	| 0 | Done |
244	| 1 | Network or server error |
245	| 2 | Usage: unknown command or option, a missing argument, a folder that does not exist |
246	| 3 | Not signed in, sign-in cancelled or expired, or the server refused the credential (401, 403) |
247	| 4 | Not found (404) |
248	| 5 | Invalid request or package: a missing `agent.json`, over a limit, a 400 or 413 |
249	| 6 | Busy: a submission already in evaluation, 3 test runs already waiting, a rate limit, or cancelling a finished run (409, 429) |
250	| 7 | `logs --follow` or `test-run --follow`: the run failed or timed out; `submit --follow`: the submission did not complete |
251	
252	With `--json`, an error is printed as `{"error": {"code", "message", "status"}}` on stdout.
253	
254	## Final private evaluation: one attempt or best of three
255	
256	The final runs your latest passed submission once, or up to three times if you opt in to **Best of 3** on your team
257	page or with `atira final --best-of 3` before the final run starts. Your best attempt counts. Details:
258	[Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#final-private-evaluation-one-attempt-or-best-of-three).
259

# The CLI

A command line for taking part: one JavaScript file for Node 24 that uses only Node's built-ins. It is made for
people and coding agents alike: every command takes `--json`, and exit codes tell outcomes apart. Everything it does
is plain HTTP, described in the [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md); you never need the CLI.

## Install

macOS and Linux:

```sh
export ATIRA_API=https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai
curl -fsSL "$ATIRA_API/install.sh" | sh
```

Windows, in PowerShell (5.1 or 7):

```powershell
$env:ATIRA_API = "https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai"
irm "$env:ATIRA_API/install.ps1" | iex
```

The script checks for Node 24 or newer. Where it is missing, it asks whether to install a private copy for atira
alone, the latest Node 24 from nodejs.org, checked against the release's `SHASUMS256.txt`. It needs no admin rights
and never changes the `node` on your `PATH`. Without a terminal to ask in, `ATIRA_INSTALL_NODE=1` says yes (`0`, no).
Then it downloads `/cli.mjs`, checks it against `/cli.mjs.sha256` and installs it for you alone, without sudo:

- macOS and Linux: the file in `~/.local/share/atira/atira.mjs`, Node (if needed) in `~/.local/share/atira/node`,
  and an `atira` command in `~/.local/bin`. It tells you when `~/.local/bin` is not on your `PATH`.
- Windows: the same under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\atira`, with `atira.cmd` in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\atira\bin`, which it adds to
  your user `PATH`. Open a new terminal afterwards.

The `atira` command runs your own Node when it is 24 or newer, else the private copy. Running the installer again
updates the CLI; it downloads Node again only when the private copy is older than 24. Read the script first, if you
like:

```sh
curl -fsSL "$ATIRA_API/install.sh" | less
```

To uninstall: `rm -rf ~/.local/share/atira ~/.local/bin/atira`, or on Windows
`Remove-Item -Recurse -Force "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\atira"`. Your sign-in stays in the config file (see below) until you
delete it.

Without installing anything, download the file and run it with Node; `node atira.mjs` works wherever this guide
says `atira`:

```sh
curl -fsSL "$ATIRA_API/cli.mjs" -o atira.mjs && node atira.mjs --help
```

The CLI talks to the server it was downloaded from. Set `ATIRA_API` to use another one. `atira upgrade` downloads the
server's current version, checks its SHA-256 and replaces the file; a download that does not match leaves the file
as it was.

## Sign in

```sh
atira login
```

The browser opens a page that asks you to sign in with GitHub, then whether to sign in the CLI on this computer.
Approve, and the browser returns to the CLI, which stores a personal token for you. The token acts as you, on the
team you are in at the time of each request: leave the team, or be removed, and it no longer reaches the team. It
lasts 90 days. Your team page lists your signed-in devices; revoke any of them there.

Where no browser can open (an SSH session, a container, a coding agent), sign in with a code instead:

```sh
atira login --device
```

waits and then stores the token. `atira login` switches to the code by itself when the browser cannot be opened, or
offers it when the browser has not answered after two minutes.

```sh
atira whoami                                  # who you are, your team, and when the token expires
atira token                                   # the token, for curl and scripts

atira logout                                  # revoke the token on the server and forget it here
```

`%USERPROFILE%\.config\atira\config.json`), readable only by you (mode 0600). `ATIRA_TOKEN` overrides it, which suits
CI and agents: `export ATIRA_TOKEN=$(atira token)`.

command that opens the page (`none` only prints the link), `--no-open` skips it, and `--json` never opens anything.

`test-run --follow` then streams the run's logs as `logs --follow` does and exits 7 if the run failed or timed out.
While the run waits for a sandbox, it prints its place in the [fair queue](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md#the-run-queue) on stderr whenever
that changes ("Queued: 3 runs ahead of yours"). With `--json --follow`, the upload's result comes as one JSON line,
then one `{"at", "stream", "text"}` line per chunk. `submit --follow` prints the review's outcome, then each scored
run's place in the queue and its end, and exits 7 unless the submission completes; with `--json`, the final
submission follows the upload's line.

`cancel <run>` takes a run (`run_...`) or a test run (`reh_...`) of your team that has not finished. The run's sandbox
is removed and the run fails with the error "Cancelled by @you"; a queued run is cancelled before it starts. Your
team can start the next test run at once. A cancelled scored run leaves its submission not complete: the leaderboard
ignores that submission, and you can submit again. A run that
has already finished answers 409 (exit 6).

`test-run` and `submit` pack the folder into a gzipped tarball the way the platform reads it:

- `agent.json` must be at the folder's root, with `run` (and optionally `setup`) as arrays of strings.
- `.git`, `node_modules` and `.DS_Store` are always left out, and so is whatever `.gitignore` files exclude (in the
  folder and below: patterns, `*`, `?`, `**`, `[...]`, a leading `/`, a trailing `/` for folders, and `!` to
  include again). Symbolic links are left out too.
- The limits are checked before uploading: at most 2,000 files, 5 MB per file, 20 MB in total, and 20 MB
  compressed (or what the server announces).

### Logs, status and the leaderboard

`package <id>` shows exactly what a run ran: the package's SHA-256 and label, its `agent.json` and every file with
its size. A scored run ran its submission's package. `--out ./downloaded` also saves the `.tar.gz` there; unpack it
with `tar -xzf <file> -C <folder>`.

`logs <run>` prints what the run has written so far; `--follow` polls with a growing pause (1 s, up to 10 s) and
exits when the run has ended. `--json` prints one `{"at", "stream", "text"}` object per line. `status` without an id
shows your best result, your latest submissions and your latest test runs.

## Configuration

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ATIRA_API` | The platform; defaults to the server the file came from |
| `ATIRA_TOKEN` | A token to use instead of the stored one |
| `ATIRA_CHALLENGE` | The default challenge |
| `ATIRA_POLL_MS` | The first pause of `logs --follow`, in milliseconds (default 1000) |
| `ATIRA_BROWSER` | The command `login`, `test-run` and `submit` open pages with, or `none` to only print the link |
| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | Where `atira/config.json` lives (default `~/.config`) |

The config file holds `{"servers": {"<ATIRA_API>": {"token": "atp_...", "token_id", "expires_at", "login"}}}`.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Done |
| 1 | Network or server error |
| 2 | Usage: unknown command or option, a missing argument, a folder that does not exist |
| 3 | Not signed in, sign-in cancelled or expired, or the server refused the credential (401, 403) |
| 4 | Not found (404) |
| 5 | Invalid request or package: a missing `agent.json`, over a limit, a 400 or 413 |
| 6 | Busy: a submission already in evaluation, 3 test runs already waiting, a rate limit, or cancelling a finished run (409, 429) |
| 7 | `logs --follow` or `test-run --follow`: the run failed or timed out; `submit --follow`: the submission did not complete |

With `--json`, an error is printed as `{"error": {"code", "message", "status"}}` on stdout.

## Final private evaluation: one attempt or best of three

The final runs your latest passed submission once, or up to three times if you opt in to **Best of 3** on your team
page or with `atira final --best-of 3` before the final run starts. Your best attempt counts. Details:
[Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md#final-private-evaluation-one-attempt-or-best-of-three).

# Agent plan and scouting notes

Findings from scouting the four public sites (public-1) and evaluating frameworks, 2026-10-10.
The private final run uses other sites, layouts and data: prompts describe roles and goals, never click paths,
and nothing below may be hardcoded into the agent.

## Framework decision

Keep the starter kit (Python 3.12, uv, Playwright 1.63) and run the worker loop on `pydantic-ai-slim[openai]`.
No browser-agent framework, no LangGraph.

- pydantic-ai 2.55 works with Qwen through the proxy (tested: tool call + typed output, thinking off, 3 s).
  It gives typed tools, typed output via an output tool (avoids the 74 s cold `json_schema` compile), validation
  retries, `UsageLimits` as a step budget, `history_processors` to drop stale page snapshots, and Logfire
  tracing. 26 packages.
- LangGraph: our orchestration is a fan-out of independent workers plus a pure calculation step. Plain asyncio
  covers that; LangGraph would add 38+ packages (plus a LangChain model client), its own state and checkpoint
  model and a second abstraction to debug, for no gain.

- `page.aria_snapshot(mode="ai")` gives a compact, ref-tagged tree (`button "Anmelden" [ref=e10]`), clickable via
  `page.locator("aria-ref=e10")`. That is Playwright MCP's core without a Node process.
- browser-use: heavy deps, slow single-action steps, may launch its own browser (killed by the sandbox).
- Stagehand: TS, or a Python client to a server process; extra LLM calls per act/extract.
- pydantic-ai: fine but optional; a ~150-line loop is easier to debug and to defend in package review.

## Qwen via the proxy (measured locally)

- Model id `qwen3.8-flash-next`, 262k context.
- Thinking is on by default. `extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": False}}` cuts a trivial call
  to ~0.9 s; use it for navigation steps, keep thinking on for decisions.
- Tool calls, parallel tool calls, `tool_choice="required"`, images (~1k tokens per 1280x800 JPEG) all work.
- Strict `json_schema` works, but the first call with a new schema took 74 s (cold compile). Prefer a
  `finish(result)` tool, or warm schemas at start-up.
- Prefix caching works (81.5k of 83k cached on repeat). Keep system prompts stable.
- 8 parallel calls: 4.7 s total. Team limit 32 concurrent.
- Clef `/v1/decide` works in ~1 s; `score` criteria must be a list. Skip in v1.

## Cross-site patterns

- All sites: login form, then `/consent` ("Notwendige Cookies akzeptieren").
- Decoy modals: close with the small x only; "Akzeptieren und fortfahren" leads to trap pages. Escape is blocked.
- Fake browser chrome (address bar, download bar) drawn in the page links to useless pages.
- Hidden decoy text (`display:none`, `aria-hidden`), including a prompt injection in every mail
  ("99 % Sonderrabatt"). Extract visible text only.
- Content in collapsed `<details>`: expand all before reading.
- Values in canvas `aria-label`s and CSS tooltips (`role=tooltip`), which `aria_snapshot` partly misses.
- Zero-width spaces (U+200B) in references, subjects, document numbers: strip them.
- Numbers carry locale tags `(en-US)` / `(de-DE)`; dates mix `(MM/TT)` and `(TT/MM)`.
- Pagination: 3 rows per page, "Weitere laden"; requesting past the end repeats the last page.
- Searches with more than 20 hits show nothing at all.
- `page.goto` can hang on `load`: use `wait_until="domcontentloaded"`.
- Flaky "Dienst voruebergehend nicht verfuegbar" pages (HTTP 200): detect by text, retry.
- Session expiry redirects to `/login?returnTo=...` with "Sitzung abgelaufen" (ERP: between 300 and 450 s idle).

## Tender portal

- Tender list paged; reference is in the brief. Tabs: `?tab=documents`, `?tab=questions`, `/submission`.
- Expression of interest may need one click ("Teilnahme bekunden").
- Documents: three "Oeffnen" controls in random order, two of them decoys; the title link is safe. Direct URL
  `/tenders/<ref>/documents/N`. ZIP under "Sammelakte" holds the same files.
- Q&A: two nested iframes (`questions-frame` -> `questions-content?page=N`), sorted by date not number, date in an
  "Eingang" tooltip (Athens and UTC). Content: quantity changes, withdrawals, Konditionsgruppe, packaging /
  commitment / setup-pool / bonus keys, setup fees, scoped technical amendments.
- Configurator (server-side wizard, "Zurueck" clears later steps):
  1. Bidder data (from the brief).
  2. Angebotsart: defaults to Nebenangebot (trap); choose Hauptangebot or Verzichtserklaerung.
  3. One page per position, shuffled order. Cascading selects (bore, stroke, mounting, certification), each needing
     its own "Auswahl uebernehmen" round trip, options sorted as text. Katalognummer options show pressure.
     Menge, Einzelpreis, collapsible Kalkulationsnachweis (base, surcharge, packaging, rebate), Lieferzeit select.
     "Position auslassen" skips. "Position hinzufuegen" adds a bogus extra position (trap).
  4. Konditionen: Rabatt and Nettosumme. A hidden `total_net` span shows the gross amount (trap).
  5. Erklaerungen: tick "Vergabeunterlagen anerkannt" only, not "Es gelten unsere AGB".
  6. Pruefen und signieren: request TAN, enter it, submit, accept `window.confirm`.
- TAN: each request invalidates the previous one; valid 5 minutes. Request, read mail, sign in one quick sequence.

## Webmail

- List and reading pane each behind a gate (slider to 100 plus "Ich bin kein Roboter"). `/messages/<id>` directly
  is simpler.
- Folders Posteingang and Archiv, searched separately. Search is AND over body too; empty search lists only TANs.
- Traps: look-alike references (`<ref>-A`), approvals for other tenders, non-approval mails from management,
  future-dated records, superseded and conditional approvals.
- Dates shown as `MM/TT`; full timestamp in `<time datetime>`.

## Supplier portal

- Spec found via the paged document list. Access gate: choose "Verbindliche Unterlagen", copy the Belegnummer
  (canvas, value in `aria-label`), tick the terms.
- Revision history collapsed; opens the oldest revision first. Status ("gueltig" / "ersetzt") only in a tooltip.
- Viewer iframe `.../viewer?revision=X&page=N`, one requirement per page. Full requirement prose in a collapsed
  "Originalwortlaut" (bore, stroke, pressure, mounting, certification, Kataloggruppe, pieces per Satz,
  nutzbarer Weg with Endreserve key).

## ERP

- After login: consent, often a flaky error page, then an unlock gate (slider, captcha box, copy Empfangsnummer).
- Only MM03, MMBE, VK13 exist; direct URLs work (`/mm03`, `/mmbe`, `/vk13?material=X`).
- Search popup `/search?transaction=..&q=..`; search the Kataloggruppe. Result rows already list most attributes,
  carton size, allocation mass vs surcharge mass, price index.
- MM03: technical tab (certification in tooltip); planning tab (status in tooltip, hidden decoy "01"; lead time
  from stock and production lead time).
- MMBE: the summary includes blocked stock (trap); use the free stock line.
- VK13: one condition record per page, older years later; validity, currency + FX key, price unit (1 or 100 ST);
  scales under `view=scales`, listed descending.
- No ordinary setup fee in the ERP; it comes from the tender Q&A.

## Architecture

```
agent/
  agent.py         orchestrator: reads run, shared findings store, starts workers, deadline (submit by T-90 s)
  llm.py           Qwen client, retry/backoff, thinking flag, usage log, stable prompts for caching
  browser_tools.py model-invoked tools (below) plus automatic overlay/gate/session handling
  extract.py       cleaned page text: visible only, details expanded, aria-labels, tooltips, iframes, no U+200B
  worker.py        generic loop: role prompt + goal + tools, step budget, deadline
  roles.py         generic role prompts: tender, spec, erp, mail
  evidence.py      pydantic records for each fact type
  calc.py          deterministic bid rules: rounding, scales, FX, packaging, setup pool, bonus (unit-tested)
  submit.py        configurator fill + TAN signing
```

Tools: `goto`, `click(ref)`, `fill(ref, text)`, `select(ref, value)`, `read_page`, `read_frame`, `next_page`,
`search(q)`, `screenshot` (fallback), `finish(result)`. Automatic: login with run credentials, consent, closing
decoy modals via x, unlocking gates, retrying flaky pages, re-login on expiry.

Fair-play line: the model chooses where to go, what to search, which revision / record / mail applies. Helpers only
extract a chosen page, paginate a chosen result set, calculate and fill forms.

## Scoring (what each version buys)

Per bid: decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, total 5, arithmetic consistency 5, withdrawn-Q&A check 5,
metal-index check 5, positions the rest (65 with both extra checks). Within each position: material 20 %,
quantity 15 %, base price 15 %, surcharge 10 %, packaging 10 %, bonus 10 %, final unit price 10 %, delivery 10 %.
Every field scores on its own, so each version adds fields and always ends with a signed bid.

## Roadmap

Each version is done when a sandbox test run (`atira test-run .`) shows the listed fields correct in the score
breakdown and finishes well under 20 minutes. Submit (`atira submit .`) after each version that beats our best.

- Tender list paged; reference is in the brief. Tabs: `?tab=documents`, `?tab=questions`, `/submission`.
- Expression of interest may need one click ("Teilnahme bekunden").
- Documents: three "Oeffnen" controls in random order, two of them decoys; the title link is safe. Direct URL
  `/tenders/<ref>/documents/N`. ZIP under "Sammelakte" holds the same files.
- Q&A: two nested iframes (`questions-frame` -> `questions-content?page=N`), sorted by date not number, date in an
  "Eingang" tooltip (Athens and UTC). Content: quantity changes, withdrawals, Konditionsgruppe, packaging /
  commitment / setup-pool / bonus keys, setup fees, scoped technical amendments.
- Configurator (server-side wizard, "Zurueck" clears later steps):
  1. Bidder data (from the brief).
  2. Angebotsart: defaults to Nebenangebot (trap); choose Hauptangebot or Verzichtserklaerung.
  3. One page per position, shuffled order. Cascading selects (bore, stroke, mounting, certification), each needing
     its own "Auswahl uebernehmen" round trip, options sorted as text. Katalognummer options show pressure.
     Menge, Einzelpreis, collapsible Kalkulationsnachweis (base, surcharge, packaging, rebate), Lieferzeit select.
     "Position auslassen" skips. "Position hinzufuegen" adds a bogus extra position (trap).
  4. Konditionen: Rabatt and Nettosumme. A hidden `total_net` span shows the gross amount (trap).
  5. Erklaerungen: tick "Vergabeunterlagen anerkannt" only, not "Es gelten unsere AGB".
  6. Pruefen und signieren: request TAN, enter it, submit, accept `window.confirm`.
- TAN: each request invalidates the previous one; valid 5 minutes. Request, read mail, sign in one quick sequence.

## Webmail

- List and reading pane each behind a gate (slider to 100 plus "Ich bin kein Roboter"). `/messages/<id>` directly
  is simpler.
- Folders Posteingang and Archiv, searched separately. Search is AND over body too; empty search lists only TANs.
- Traps: look-alike references (`<ref>-A`), approvals for other tenders, non-approval mails from management,
  future-dated records, superseded and conditional approvals.
- Dates shown as `MM/TT`; full timestamp in `<time datetime>`.

## Supplier portal

- Spec found via the paged document list. Access gate: choose "Verbindliche Unterlagen", copy the Belegnummer
  (canvas, value in `aria-label`), tick the terms.
- Revision history collapsed; opens the oldest revision first. Status ("gueltig" / "ersetzt") only in a tooltip.
- Viewer iframe `.../viewer?revision=X&page=N`, one requirement per page. Full requirement prose in a collapsed
  "Originalwortlaut" (bore, stroke, pressure, mounting, certification, Kataloggruppe, pieces per Satz,
  nutzbarer Weg with Endreserve key).

## ERP

- After login: consent, often a flaky error page, then an unlock gate (slider, captcha box, copy Empfangsnummer).
- Only MM03, MMBE, VK13 exist; direct URLs work (`/mm03`, `/mmbe`, `/vk13?material=X`).
- Search popup `/search?transaction=..&q=..`; search the Kataloggruppe. Result rows already list most attributes,
  carton size, allocation mass vs surcharge mass, price index.
- MM03: technical tab (certification in tooltip); planning tab (status in tooltip, hidden decoy "01"; lead time
  from stock and production lead time).
- MMBE: the summary includes blocked stock (trap); use the free stock line.
- VK13: one condition record per page, older years later; validity, currency + FX key, price unit (1 or 100 ST);
  scales under `view=scales`, listed descending.
- No ordinary setup fee in the ERP; it comes from the tender Q&A.

## Architecture

```
agent/
  agent.py         orchestrator: reads run, shared findings store, starts workers, deadline (submit by T-90 s)
  llm.py           Qwen client, retry/backoff, thinking flag, usage log, stable prompts for caching
  browser_tools.py model-invoked tools (below) plus automatic overlay/gate/session handling
  extract.py       cleaned page text: visible only, details expanded, aria-labels, tooltips, iframes, no U+200B
  worker.py        generic loop: role prompt + goal + tools, step budget, deadline
  roles.py         generic role prompts: tender, spec, erp, mail
  evidence.py      pydantic records for each fact type
  calc.py          deterministic bid rules: rounding, scales, FX, packaging, setup pool, bonus (unit-tested)
  submit.py        configurator fill + TAN signing
```

Tools: `goto`, `click(ref)`, `fill(ref, text)`, `select(ref, value)`, `read_page`, `read_frame`, `next_page`,
`search(q)`, `screenshot` (fallback), `finish(result)`. Automatic: login with run credentials, consent, closing
decoy modals via x, unlocking gates, retrying flaky pages, re-login on expiry.

Fair-play line: the model chooses where to go, what to search, which revision / record / mail applies. Helpers only
extract a chosen page, paginate a chosen result set, calculate and fill forms.

## Scoring (what each version buys)

Per bid: decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, total 5, arithmetic consistency 5, withdrawn-Q&A check 5,
metal-index check 5, positions the rest (65 with both extra checks). Within each position: material 20 %,
quantity 15 %, base price 15 %, surcharge 10 %, packaging 10 %, bonus 10 %, final unit price 10 %, delivery 10 %.
Every field scores on its own, so each version adds fields and always ends with a signed bid.

## Roadmap

Each version is done when a sandbox test run (`atira test-run .`) shows the listed fields correct in the score
breakdown and finishes well under 20 minutes. Submit (`atira submit .`) after each version that beats our best.

{
  "setup": ["uv", "sync"],
  "run": ["uv", "run", "--no-sync", "python", "agent.py"],
  "models": ["qwen"]
}
"""
v0 check: one worker per website, each signs in and reads one page it chooses, in parallel.

Run from the repo root with the scouting logins and the models proxy:
    eval "$(atira scout --env)"; HEADLESS=1 uv run --project agent python dev/smoke.py [siteId ...]
"""
import asyncio
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "agent"))

from playwright.async_api import async_playwright  # noqa: E402
from pydantic import BaseModel  # noqa: E402

### v0: harness (half a day)

- `llm.py`: pydantic-ai model for Qwen, thinking on/off settings, retries, usage logging.
- `extract.py`: cleaned page text (visible only, details expanded, aria-labels, tooltips, iframes, no U+200B).
- `browser_tools.py`: goto, click, fill, select, read_page, next_page, finish; automatic consent, decoy-modal
  close, gate unlock, flaky-page retry, re-login on expiry.
- `worker.py`: one pydantic-ai Agent per role, deps = page + findings store, step budget, deadline.
- Trace log per run (steps, tool calls, tokens, seconds) to see where time goes.
- Done when: a worker logs into each of the four scouting sites and reads one chosen page correctly.

### v1: eligible signed bid (~10 to 15 points)

- Tender worker: reference, positions with units, bidder data from the brief.
- Configurator: Hauptangebot, omit every position, discount 0, total 0, decline AGB, request TAN.
- Mail worker: newest TAN, then sign and accept the confirm, all within the TAN's 5 minutes.
- Done when: reference and decision correct, the run is eligible.

### v2: materials, quantities, delivery (~+30)

- Tender worker reads the Q&A: quantity changes, withdrawals (withdrawn-Q&A check), Satz positions.
- Spec worker: current revision, requirement per position, Kataloggruppe, pieces per Satz.
- ERP worker: Kataloggruppe search, exact attribute match, active status; stock and both lead times.
- `calc.py`: final quantities, shared-stock rule, lead time; no_bid when a material is missing.
- Configurator fills material, quantity, lead time; price fields still blank or omitted per field.
- Done when: material, quantity, delivery correct per position.

### v3: prices, discount, totals (~+25)

- ERP worker: condition record valid on the scenario date, scales, price unit, currency + FX key.
- Mail worker: director approvals (exact reference, latest, conditional threshold), Devisenfixing.
- `calc.py`: base price with FX, discount clauses default rule, final unit price, total, HALF_UP everywhere.
- Done when: base price, discount, final unit price, total and arithmetic consistency correct.

### v4: clause rules (remaining points)

- Konditionsgruppen + Konditionsregeln (discount scope per position).
- Scoped amendments + Technikfreigabe (nutzbarer Weg) before material matching.
- Metal index (validity window) for the mass surcharge; packaging tariffs and cartons; Terminfreigabe
  commitments; Ruestpools shared setup with cent allocation; Projektbonus bands with largest-remainder split.
- Done when: every field in the breakdown is correct on public-1.

### v5: speed, cost, generalisation

- Four browsers, one per site, workers start as soon as their inputs are known.
- Thinking only on decision steps, trimmed snapshots, stable prompts for cache hits.
- Hard deadline guard: sign whatever is ready by T-90 s.
- Generalisation check: prompts and helpers contain no site names, URLs, field labels or values; helpers detect
  patterns (consent buttons, modals, sliders) generically. The private run uses other software and layouts.
- Optional: a stronger model with a team key only for steps the breakdown shows Qwen getting wrong.

## Working rules

- `calc.py` gets unit tests from the bid rules with invented numbers; it is pure and model-free.
- Hand-derived public-1 expectations live outside `agent/` (e.g. `checks/`), never in the package: the package
  reviewer rejects anything that looks like a stored answer.
- Split work by worker: tender + configurator, mail, spec, ERP, calc can be built in parallel against the
  findings store's pydantic records.

# CLAUDE.md

Team error404.ai at the Atira EHL Challenge ("From RFQ to bid", challenge id `rfq`, event 10 Oct 2026, up to 5 people
per team). The agent lives in `agent/` and is built on the Atira starter kit. Keep the GitHub repo private.

## Status and layout

- `docs/plan.md`: framework decision (pydantic-ai on Qwen, no LangGraph, no browser-agent framework), module layout,
  site scouting notes and the roadmap v0 to v5. Read it first. Its scouting notes describe public-1 only: they inform
  generic helpers, they must never become hardcoded paths, labels, values or prompt text (the private final run uses
  other software, layouts and data).
- `agent/`: starter kit (`run.py`, `browsers.py`, `models.py`, `agent.py` with the `solve()` stub) plus the new harness
  modules `llm.py`, `extract.py`, `browser_tools.py`, `worker.py`, `tracing.py`. Planned, not yet present: `roles.py`,
  `evidence.py`, `calc.py`, `submit.py`. `agent.json` has no `browsers` key yet (default 1; the plan wants 4).
- `dev/smoke.py`: the v0 check (one worker per site logs in and reads a page). From the repo root:
  `eval "$(atira scout --env)"; HEADLESS=1 uv run --project agent python dev/smoke.py [siteId ...]`
- Next: finish v0, then v1 (a signed, eligible bid), then v2 to v4 for field points. Use `git status` and
  `atira status` for the current state; do not trust dated numbers in this file.

## Platform docs (source of truth; re-read, they change)

Base `https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai`. Public pages (home, start, challenge, leaderboard, team profiles) are also
Markdown via `.md`; docs are `/docs/<name>.md`.

- `/start.md`, `/challenges/rfq.md` (29 bid rules, answer schema), `/challenges/rfq/leaderboard.md`
- `/docs/fair-play.md`, `scoring.md`, `submitting.md`, `run-contract.md`, `building-an-agent.md`, `cli.md`, `api.md`,
  `mcp.md`, `faq.md`, `demo-day.md`; `/openapi.json`, `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt` (all docs in one file)
- Announcements need a token: `curl -H "x-api-key: $(atira token)" https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/v1/announcements`
- Submission deadline and prizes are not in the docs: ask the organizers. Demo day: best teams run live on stage, so
  keep a one-line start command (`atira test-run ./agent`) and a fallback recording.

The scouting logins are deliberately NOT stored here: run `atira scout`. Never write them, or anything copied from
the sites, into code, prompts, fixtures, notes or fallbacks.

## Fair play (an AI reviewer rejects or flags these)

- No hardcoded scenario values (tender refs, material numbers, prices, discounts, logins, TANs), not even as defaults,
  fallbacks or in prompts. Facts the brief states for every scenario (e.g. the sales director's mailbox) are fine.
- No pre-solving, by you or an AI assistant, put into the package. Hand-derived expectations stay outside `agent/`.
- Must be agentic: a model chooses where to go, what to search and what matters. Rejected: a fixed click path (model
  unused or only a fallback), or a crawler/helper that gathers all evidence before model-directed investigation.
  Allowed helpers: parse a page or document the model chose, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate,
  validate, retry, fill forms. Several agents and parallel browsers are fine.
- Only the platform API, the four sites and the model proxy; no local models; no own browsers in the sandbox (use the
  provided 1 to 4, tabs and contexts are free).
- Do not write notes meant to steer the reviewer. Outcomes: passed; flagged (runs, but hidden from the leaderboard
  until an organizer passes it); rejected (no runs).

## The task and its traps

One signed bid, entered in the tender portal's configurator and signed with a TAN from the webmail. Site ids are
public-1 names; the private set renames and re-splits sites, so never branch code on siteId, URL or layout.

| Site | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| Tender portal | Tender, bill of quantities, bidder Q&A (the hub: quantity changes, withdrawals, scoped spec amendments, Konditionsgruppe, packaging, commitment and setup-pool keys), configurator |
| Supplier portal | Buyer's spec and revisions (oldest shown first; use the one marked current) |
| ERP | Materials and status, stock, lead times, price conditions with validity and scales, pieces per carton, allocation mass |
| Webmail | Director's discount approval, TAN, authority mails (look-alikes, superseded, archive) |

Read all 29 rules in `challenges/rfq.md` before writing prompts or tools. Highest-impact traps:

- **Authority and time (21):** per key, the latest record dated no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender
  reference, from the right sender (technik, logistik, finanzen, kalkulation + bidder mailbox domain). Future-dated and
  unrelated records never apply; a failed condition does not revive an older record.
- **no_bid (3, 8, 16):** if any position has no exactly matching active material (after amendments and the "nutzbarer
  Weg" derivation, rule 20), send `no_bid`, no positions, `total_net` 0 (schema still requires `discount_percent`; a
  conditional approval means 0 %). Omitting positions is not a substitute (rule 9).
- **Sign and submit:** saving alone scores nothing. Partial bids use "Position auslassen" and are still signed.
- **Per position vs per material:** price scales per position; stock pooled per material (15); delivery commitments
  per position, only if the material matches and pooled demand is within the inclusive ceiling (24).
- **Rounding:** HALF_UP, at the steps the rules name: FX-converted base price to cents (22), discount threshold and
  bonus aggregate to cents (16, 26), then the final unit price once from unrounded per-piece components (27).
  Breakdown fields are reports, not inputs. Bonus split: largest remainders (26); setup pool: the cent-allocation rule
  stated in the Ruestpools mail (25).
- **Reporting:** `surcharge_per_unit` is before discount and covers mass surcharge plus ordinary and allocated setup;
  setup and packaging are never discounted; blank = unanswered, `0.00` = known zero; `rebate_total` is per position.
- **Conditional discount (16):** threshold uses undiscounted scale prices, no surcharge or setup, inclusive; on failure
  0 %, never an older approval. Metal index: the rate whose window contains the scenario date (28).
- Positions are matched by number; extras or duplicates cost one position's share; money is compared to the cent.

## Runs, ranking, winning

Details live in `submitting.md`, `run-contract.md`, `scoring.md`, `faq.md`. What bites:

- Test run (`atira test-run ./agent --follow`): 2 h, public data, shows per-part points, never on the leaderboard.
  Scored (`atira submit ./agent`): AI review, then one 20-minute run, one submission in flight per team (else 429).
- Time runs from the start of the run command to the accepted answer. 202 is final (even if wrong); 400 lists issues
  and the clock keeps running; validate against `answer_schema` first. Submit about 90 s before `expires_at` (the kit's
  `run.seconds_left` helps); platform docs only say "about a minute". A run without an answer scores 0.
- Setup has network and 5 min (untimed), but no run variables or secrets, and nothing it starts survives. The timed run
  reaches only the platform, sites and model proxy (`HTTP(S)_PROXY`, honour it in custom clients). Send your own
  User-Agent (default Python agents get 403 "Error 1010").
- `agent.json`: `setup`, `run`, `models` (list every hosted model used, e.g. `["qwen","clef"]`), `browsers` 1 to 4.
  Package: 20 MB compressed and uncompressed, 2,000 files, 5 MB per file, `.gitignore` honoured, no secrets inside.
  Own model keys are team secrets (names: capitals, digits, underscore, letter first, max 20, no platform names).
- Order: eligible (right tender reference), then quality 0 to 100, then lower cost x time (floors $0.01, 1 s). A wrong
  bid/no_bid decision costs quality, not eligibility (75 of 100 in a no_bid case). Weights: rule 29.
- Winners: private-dataset final run of our LATEST submission that PASSED review (not the best), then public
  leaderboard, then elegance. So: never tune to public-1; every passing `atira submit` replaces the final candidate,
  even a worse one, so confirm with the team first. `atira final --best-of 3` (before the final starts) allows three
  attempts (own-key cost up to 3x); private runs show no score breakdown.
- Models: hosted Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`QWEN_BASE_URL/KEY`, 32 concurrent) and Clef (`CLEF_*`, 16 concurrent) are free
  but add a SIMULATED price to run cost; own-key calls are metered at provider prices through the proxy. Measured
  Qwen behaviour (thinking flag, schema cold start, caching) is in `docs/plan.md`.

## Dev loop

```sh
curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.sh | sh    # CLI; the installer provides Node 24 if missing
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" && atira login           # `atira upgrade` if a command is unknown
(cd agent && uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium)
atira models proxy                       # terminal 1 (port 8765)
eval "$(atira scout --env)"              # terminal 2: scouting logins + model vars
(cd agent && uv run --no-sync python agent.py)   # local run, nothing submitted
(cd agent && uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests)
atira test-run ./agent --dry-run         # what would upload
atira test-run ./agent --follow          # sandbox run with score breakdown
```

Debugging: `atira logs <run> --follow`, `atira status [id]`, `atira package <id> --out dir`, `atira cancel <run>`; every
command takes `--json`. `claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp` gives `diagnose_run`, `run_logs`, `run_llm_calls`,
`run_screenshot`, `compare_runs` and more (`mcp.md`). Use the score breakdown to localise errors (zero surcharge
points can come from mass surcharge, setup or metal index inputs). A cancelled scored run ends its submission (ignored
by the leaderboard), so you may resubmit. Missing "OpenAI key" 401s mean no provider key arrived (team secret).
On macOS, python.org Python needs `Install Certificates.command` or `SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/cert.pem`.

## Team conventions

- Git: commit author `josteng <jonas@stenglein.dev>`; imperative subject of at most 50 characters, body as short `-`
  bullets; no attribution trailers (no Co-Authored-By, no session links); never stage anything under `.claude/`;
  never push or open a PR without asking first.
- Never put real credentials, personal data or site values in tests, fixtures, docs or comments; invent placeholders.

  reference, from the right sender (technik, logistik, finanzen, kalkulation + bidder mailbox domain). Future-dated and
  unrelated records never apply; a failed condition does not revive an older record.
- **no_bid (3, 8, 16):** if any position has no exactly matching active material (after amendments and the "nutzbarer
  Weg" derivation, rule 20), send `no_bid`, no positions, `total_net` 0 (schema still requires `discount_percent`; a
  conditional approval means 0 %). Omitting positions is not a substitute (rule 9).

- **Per position vs per material:** price scales per position; stock pooled per material (15); delivery commitments
  per position, only if the material matches and pooled demand is within the inclusive ceiling (24).
- **Rounding:** HALF_UP, at the steps the rules name: FX-converted base price to cents (22), discount threshold and
  bonus aggregate to cents (16, 26), then the final unit price once from unrounded per-piece components (27).

Details live in `submitting.md`, `run-contract.md`, `scoring.md`, `faq.md`. What bites:

  Scored (`atira submit ./agent`): AI review, then one 20-minute run, one submission in flight per team (else 429).
- Time runs from the start of the run command to the accepted answer. 202 is final (even if wrong); 400 lists issues
  and the clock keeps running; validate against `answer_schema` first. Submit about 90 s before `expires_at` (the kit's
  `run.seconds_left` helps); platform docs only say "about a minute". A run without an answer scores 0.

  bid/no_bid decision costs quality, not eligibility (75 of 100 in a no_bid case). Weights: rule 29.

  but add a SIMULATED price to run cost; own-key calls are metered at provider prices through the proxy. Measured

+by the leaderboard), so you may resubmit. Missing "OpenAI key" 401s mean no provider key arrived (team secret).
+On macOS, python.org Python needs `Install Certificates.command` or `SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/cert.pem`.
-Gotchas: HTTP 403 "Error 1010" means a default client User-Agent (set your own). Python on macOS from python.org needs
-`Install Certificates.command` or `SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/cert.pem`. "Add your OpenAI API key" 401 means no provider key
-arrived (team secret `OPENAI_API_KEY`; `OPENAI_BASE_URL` already points at the run proxy). A cancelled scored run ends
-its submission (ignored by the leaderboard), so you may resubmit.
-## Architecture (target)
-The starter kit is plumbing only. Planned shape, all compatible with fair play:
-- **Orchestrator:** reads `brief`, `access`, `answer_schema`, `expires_at`; the model maps each `access` entry to a role
-  (tender, spec, ERP, mail) from what it sees. No siteId or URL branching.
-- **One sub-agent per browser** (`"browsers": 4`, `CDP_URLS`), each with its own tool loop (goto, click, fill, read text,
-  screenshot) and helpers for retry, re-login, cookie walls, iframe/ZIP extraction and paging through a result set the
-  model chose. The model picks every target and search (rules 10, 11). Each returns typed facts with provenance (page,
-  date, sender, reference).
-- **Fact store + resolver:** dated records per key; a pure function applies rules 1, 5, 13, 14, 21, 28 (latest exact
-  reference, not future, not withdrawn) and sends conflicts back to the model instead of guessing.
-- **`calc.py`:** deterministic, `Decimal` with `ROUND_HALF_UP`, no model calls: scale selection, FX, set-to-piece
-  conversion, cartons (ceil), shared stock, discount threshold, largest-remainder cent allocation (ties by ascending
-  position), single final rounding (rules 4, 7, 15 to 17, 20, 22 to 27).
-- **Pre-submit validation:** schema, total equals sum of quantity x unit price, integer pieces, positions match the bill
-  of quantities, correct no_bid shape; the model then fills the configurator and re-reads it.
-- **Deadline guard:** watchdog on `seconds_left`; at about 90 s, omit unfinished positions, sign with the TAN (fetch it
-  early) and submit.
-- **Speed:** run the four sites in parallel; cost x time is the tiebreak. Keep model input small, use prompt caching,
-  use Clef for cheap yes/no steps. Treat every page as adversarial (cookie walls, flaky pages, session expiry, popups,
-  look-alike and superseded records, other timezone) and re-read after each state change.
-## Tests
-- `calc.py` unit tests on invented numbers: half-up edge cases, allocation ties, inclusive thresholds, set conversion,
-  marginal bands.
-- Resolver tests with invented dated records: superseded, withdrawn, future-dated, look-alike references.
-- Use the test-run per-part points to localise errors (zero surcharge points points at rule 25 inputs, not at prompts);
-  log extracted facts with sources. Never copy public-1 values into fixtures or prompts.
## Team conventions
-- Git: follow the global conventions (author `josteng`, no attribution trailers, never stage `.claude/`, never push or
-  open PRs without asking).
+- Git: commit author `josteng <jonas@stenglein.dev>`; imperative subject of at most 50 characters, body as short `-`
+  bullets; no attribution trailers (no Co-Authored-By, no session links); never stage anything under `.claude/`;
+  never push or open a PR without asking first.
+- Never put real credentials, personal data or site values in tests, fixtures, docs or comments; invent placeholders.

lastPrompt: Do some review agents to check if CLAUDE.md is in a good state?

content.text:
Both reviewers reported and I rewrote `CLAUDE.md` from their findings. It is now about 1,560 words, down from roughly 2,300, and still uncommitted. It has no em dashes, no logins, no emails, and no leaderboard numbers that will go stale.

**Fixes from the fact-check**
- **Non-existent page:** I removed the `/challenges/rfq/stage` link, which appears in no doc.
- **Markdown claim:** only the public pages, not every page, are available as Markdown.
- **no_bid and discount:** it no longer says a no_bid answer sets discount 0. Only a conditional approval gives 0 %, and the schema still requires `discount_percent`.
- **Rounding:** it said "round only at the end", which contradicts rule 22. It now follows the rules: round the FX base price to cents, then the threshold and bonus aggregate, then the final unit price once from unrounded components.
- **Allocation:** largest-remainder applies to the project bonus. The setup pool uses the rule stated in the Rüstpools mail.
- **Which submissions count:** only a submission that passes review replaces the final candidate.
- **Simulated prices:** these apply to the hosted models only. Own-key calls are metered at the providers' prices.
- **Limits and rules:**
  - Team-secret naming rules are now stated.
  - The package also has a 20 MB uncompressed limit.
  - The deadline margin is one number (about 90 s) instead of two.
  - Items that come only from the starter kit are labelled as such.

**Changes from the usability review**
- **Status section first:** a new "Status and layout" section lists the new modules in `agent/`, points to `docs/plan.md` and `dev/smoke.py`, and names the next step: finish v0, then v1, a signed eligible bid.
- **Plan warning:** the plan's scouting notes may inform generic helpers but must never be hardcoded.
- **Config gap:** `agent.json` has no `browsers` key yet.
- **Shrunk to links:** the runs table, models section, architecture section and debugging detail now point to the docs and `docs/plan.md`.
- **Git rules:** they are written out in full, since teammates don't have your global file.

I left `docs/plan.md`, `dev/` and the new `agent/` modules alone. They aren't mine, so someone else is working in the repo. The two reviewers disagreed on one point: the plan has role workers while my old file had one agent per browser. I deferred to the plan.
